fixture_name: McGrath Hwy (Rte 28) @ Mystic Ave/Broadway — real US design-stage RSA (MassDOT/HNTB)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Dysfunctional pedestrian signals at a high-volume arterial crossing pose a real, substantive safety hazard for pedestrians and is squarely relevant to the scheme's safety context at preliminary design.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal deficiency claim is anchored by a verbatim quoted record (EV-US-034: 'Investigate and fix existing dysfunctional pedestrian signals') tied to the recorded safety-issue table for this location.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern under FHWA RSA semantics with no conflation of compliance questions; addressing existing conditions bearing on user safety is legitimate at the design stage.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific (intersection, pedestrian indications), actionable (investigate and repair before design progresses), and viable within the current stage; not null or vague.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians—the affected vulnerable road users—are explicitly identified as the exposed group and the exposure scenario is built around their reliance on the displays.

justifications.substance: Concrete, scheme-relevant compliance scope covering five named pedestrian access elements (markings, refuge island sizing, detectable warnings, APS, countdown signals) against mandatory AAB/ADA Standards at audited intersections.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-US-035 supplies a verbatim quote of the enhancement-list entry that directly supports the pivotal claim; the statement restates the recorded entry without invention.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a normative conformance question with risk components nulled, keeping the AAB/ADA compliance issue categorically distinct from any safety severity/likelihood judgment per FHWA RSA semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific (all pedestrian crossings, enumerated elements), actionable ('within the current design' at preliminary design stage), and viable for the design team to incorporate.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians—the core VRU group—are the explicit focus, with their crossing, refuge, detection, and signal needs comprehensively addressed across all listed elements.
